neighbours.label: Verb of a physical flux (light, water, particles, gas) striking, entering or passing through a surface or medium
fire: A photon striking the retina triggers a chemical change in the rod cell.
Groundwater seeping into the tunnel had to be pumped out every night.
When the laser beam hits the mirror, part of it passes straight through.
Cosmic rays penetrate the hull and leave tracks in the detector.
Sound waves entering the ear canal set the eardrum vibrating.
Hot gas escaping through the vent cooled as it crossed the chamber.
Rainwater percolating through the limestone dissolves it slowly.
X-rays passing through soft tissue reach the film almost unhindered.
quiet: A chemist studying the retina described a change in the rod cell.
Workers walking into the tunnel had to be counted every night.
When the technician adjusts the mirror, part of it points straight up.
Astronauts inspect the hull and leave notes in the logbook.
A nurse entering the clinic set the bell ringing.
The gas bill arriving in the post was higher than expected.
The guide describing the limestone explained how it formed.
Patients waiting in the clinic reached the desk almost immediately.
